title: SkillBridge Starter Toolkit
tagline: These are the free tools two high schoolers used to land internships and build a network, with no paywalls and no trials that start charging you two weeks later.
intro: Every tool here was free when we checked in June 2026. When "free" comes with a catch, like needing a library card, we say so. The "free" tools that turn out to be traps are listed at the bottom.

sections.title: Get experience (when you have none yet)

items.name: Forage
items.body: free virtual job simulations from real companies; do intern-style tasks in a few hours and earn a certificate for your resume/LinkedIn; no application, 16+.

items.name: Start your own thing
items.body: a club, project, or event at your school; "founder" beats "member" on every application; free, ungatekeepable.

items.name: Your city's Summer Youth Employment Program
items.body: many cities run paid teen summer jobs; search "[your city] summer youth employment"; free to apply, usually paid.

sections.title: Get certified (free certs you can list)

items.name: HubSpot Academy
items.body: employer-recognized marketing/sales/content certs, a few hours each; certs + exams 100% free.

items.name: freeCodeCamp
items.body: free coding certs (web design, JavaScript, Python), built around projects and shareable; nonprofit, no paywall or card.

items.name: Google Skillshop
items.body: free Google Ads & Analytics certs from Google.

items.name: LinkedIn Learning
items.body: 16,000+ courses, free with a public library card (free digital card available online in minutes), completion certs.

items.name: Khan Academy
items.body: free academic lessons + a careers section; nonprofit.

items.name: Coursera
items.body: audit almost any university course free (you get the lessons without a certificate); cert costs money unless you apply for financial aid.

items.name: FlowCV
items.body: clean ATS-friendly resumes (they work with automated application screening), unlimited watermark-free PDF downloads, no trial/card/paywall; first resume free forever.

items.name: Google Docs
items.body: simplest free option; free resume templates → PDF.

items.name: Canva
items.body: free for visual portfolios/mockups/graphics; use FlowCV or Docs for your resume (Canva's fancy templates can confuse application scanners).

items.name: Indeed
items.body: biggest job board; filter for part-time/entry-level jobs to find teen-friendly roles.

items.name: Named programs worth knowing
items.body: NASA High School Internships (16+), Microsoft High School Discovery Program (paid), and similar programs run every summer; competitive, but open to high schoolers; search the program name + "high school."

items.name: Forage (again)
items.body: when you can't land a formal internship yet, a finished simulation is the next best resume line.

items.name: LinkedIn
items.body: free, and the most useful account a high schooler can make; opportunities come through people, and this is where they are.
Pair it with LinkedIn Learning above, and follow us for posts on setting up a profile that isn't empty, messaging strangers without being awkward, and getting replies.

traps.title: ⚠️ "Free" tools that turn out to be traps

items.body: Zety, Resume Genius, Resume.io — cheap trials that auto-renew to ~$24–26 every four weeks; use FlowCV instead.
If a "free" tool wants a credit card before you've made anything, close the tab.

outroLead: This is the shortlist we recommend.
outroDiscord: New guides go out in The SkillBridge Brief.
